summary: Page 6 report headlined 'Final settlement: plain language from Truthful James A. Bradley,' on a mass meeting of Black residents at Marrow's Hall in Asbury Park protesting pavilion signs posted by resort founder James A. Bradley barring Black people from certain beach pavilions. Speakers debated segregation, property rights, and the town's treatment of Black workers and visitors. The page also carries a note that the first issue of the Monmouth edition of the New Jersey Trumpet, a Newark-based Black newspaper published by Colonel William Murrell, had just reached the office, edited locally by Rev. Fillmore Smith.
